report:
# Research Findings: Olive Oil and Stroke Risk

Based on the available evidence, the claim that "consuming more olive oil reduces the risk of stroke" is **well-supported**, not false — though the strength of evidence varies by study type.

**Randomized controlled trial evidence (strongest):** The PREDIMED trial, a large randomized primary prevention trial, found that a Mediterranean diet supplemented with extra-virgin olive oil (or nuts) reduced major cardiovascular events compared to a control diet, with the benefit "particularly" driven by reduced stroke incidence (https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/pdf/10.1161/hypertensionaha.113.03353). This is significant because RCTs provide stronger causal evidence than observational cohorts.

**Meta-analyses of cohort/case-control studies:** A meta-analysis by Martínez-González and colleagues found each 25g/day increment in olive oil intake was associated with a 24% reduced relative risk of stroke (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/261954820_Olive_oil_consumption_and_risk_of_CHD_andor_stroke_A_meta-analysis_of_case-control_cohort_and_intervention_studies).

**Some inconsistency exists:** Not all analyses agree — one source notes "a 2020 meta-analysis found no significant link between olive oil intake and stroke risk" (https://www.healthline.com/nutrition/11-proven-benefits-of-olive-oil), suggesting the evidence isn't uniformly conclusive across all meta-analyses.

**Confounding concerns:** Some coverage cautions that in certain cohorts, olive oil intake was low and other Mediterranean diet components (vegetables, fruits, whole grains) may have driven much of the protective effect, meaning olive oil's independent contribution could be overstated in observational data (https://www.aol.com/articles/happens-stroke-risk-mediterranean-diet-234205542.html).

**Conclusion:** The weight of evidence — especially the randomized PREDIMED trial plus multiple meta-analyses — supports a real protective association between olive oil and stroke risk, though effect sizes vary and some studies find null results, and disentangling olive oil from overall dietary pattern remains challenging.
